mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series 340i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 3 Series 340i engine replacement typically costs between £2,500 and £7,500 supply-only, depending on the condition type and variant. Used engines: £2,500-£4,500. Reconditioned engines: £3,800-£6,000. Rebuilt engines: £4,500-£7,500 with 12-month warranty. Supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,200 in labour.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the BMW 340i and M340i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 340i (F30, 2015-2018) uses the B58B30M0 engine producing 326 bhp and is the standard performance petrol model. The M340i (G20, 2019-present) uses the higher-output B58B30O1 engine producing 374-382 bhp, with revised suspension, brakes, and an M Sport differential as standard. Both share the same B58 engine family, but the M340i represents a significant step up in performance and chassis tuning.

mainEntity.name: Is the B58 engine reliable in the BMW 340i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the B58 is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern engines. It has won multiple Ward's 10 Best Engines awards and is praised for its robust closed-deck aluminium block design. However, like any engine, it has known issues - coolant leaks, oil filter housing gasket leaks, and PCV valve failures are the most common. Regular maintenance and early intervention prevent these from becoming major problems.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of a failing PCV valve in a BMW 340i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common signs of PCV valve failure in the B58 engine are: rough idle or engine misfires, oil in the intake or charge pipe, and check engine light with lean condition codes. If you notice any of these symptoms, get the PCV valve inspected by a specialist.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series 340i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 3 Series 340i engine replacement takes 2-4 working days. F30 (2015-2018): 10-14 hours labour - around 2-3 days. G20 M340i (2019-present): 10-14 hours labour - around 2-3 days. Supply-only engines can be delivered nationwide within 1-2 working days. Full supply & fit typically adds 1-2 days for booking and workshop scheduling.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt BMW 3 Series 340i engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every rebuilt BMW 3 Series 340i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty as standard. The warranty covers manufacturing defects and parts failure. Upgraded components address the original failure points. Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series 340i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 340i arrived in 2015 as the flagship petrol model of the F30 3 Series, replacing the 335i and introducing the all-new B58 engine. The B58 - a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six - represented a significant leap forward from the N55, with a closed-deck aluminium block, a single twin-scroll turbocharger, and air-to-liquid intercooling. It has since won multiple Ward's 10 Best Engines awards and is widely regarded as one of BMW's finest modern powerplants.

milestones.description: B58B30M0, 3.0-litre straight-six turbo (326 bhp / 240 kW) - F30 generation launched, replaced the N55-powered 335i
B58B30O1, 3.0-litre straight-six turbo (374 bhp / 275 kW) - Higher-output version for later applications
B58B30O1, 3.0-litre straight-six turbo (382 bhp) - G20 M340i generation, updated with mild-hybrid technology
B58B30M2, 3.0-litre straight-six turbo (386 bhp) - LCI update, increased power and torque

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series 340i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 3 Series 340i's B58 engine is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern powerplants - but it's not immune to age-related issues. Coolant leaks, oil filter housing gasket failures, and valve cover gasket deterioration are the most common concerns. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant Leaks - Why the BMW 3 Series 340i B58 Engine Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: The B58's water-to-air intercooler uses seals that can degrade over time, leading to coolant leaks. The water pump and thermostat housing are also known failure points.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace intercooler seals, pressure test system
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with no overheating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump and thermostat housing
Supply & fit, fully rebuilt B58 unit, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If engine has overheated and sustained damage

For F30 examples under £10,000, a used engine or targeted repair may be more appropriate. For G20 cars, a rebuilt engine with warranty is a straightforward decision given the vehicle's value.
problems.recommendation: For B58 340i owners, preventative cooling system maintenance is the smart play. Replacing the water pump and thermostat housing at 60,000 miles costs far less than an engine replacement if a leak leads to overheating. Regularly check coolant levels and inspect for visible puddles under the vehicle.

problems.group: Oil Filter Housing and Valve Cover Gasket Leaks
problems.h4: Oil Filter Housing and Valve Cover Gasket Leaks - Why the BMW 3 Series 340i B58 Engine Leaks Oil
problems.rootCause: The oil filter housing gasket and valve cover gasket deteriorate over time due to heat cycling, leading to oil seeping out. If left unaddressed, oil pressure can drop, potentially causing more significant engine problems.

repairOptions.longevity: If oil spots under vehicle or burning oil smell is present
If oil leaks onto exhaust manifold causing burning smell
If oil pressure drop has caused bearing damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For F30 340i owners, gasket replacements are routine maintenance and well within the value of the car. Addressing them early prevents more costly engine damage. For G20 M340i owners, the same principle applies - these are maintenance items, not replacement triggers.
problems.recommendation: If you notice oil spots under your BMW 340i or smell burning oil, get the gaskets inspected immediately. Replacing the oil filter housing and valve cover gaskets at a specialist costs £300-£800 combined - a fraction of the cost of an engine replacement. Don't ignore oil leaks; they can lead to low oil pressure and catastrophic engine failure.

problems.group: PCV Valve and VANOS Solenoid Issues
problems.h4: PCV Valve and VANOS Solenoid Issues - Why the BMW 3 Series 340i B58 Engine Misfires or Idles Roughly
problems.rootCause: The B58's PCV valve can fail, particularly on cars with upgraded turbos, causing misfires and rough idle. VANOS solenoid O-rings degrade over time, affecting variable valve timing.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace PCV valve, clean intake system
repairOptions.longevity: If rough idle or misfires are present
If rough idle or reduced power is present

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Both repairs are routine maintenance for any B58 340i and are well within the value of the car.
problems.recommendation: PCV valve and VANOS solenoid issues are relatively inexpensive to fix if caught early. A specialist can diagnose and replace these components for £200-£500. Don't ignore rough idle or misfires - they can indicate deeper issues if left unaddressed.
